buyer_goals.statement: Renewal of the platform because it is central to access control, with the next phase reducing exceptions that create audit noise
Reduce regional exceptions and ensure every exception becomes a governance conversation rather than informal workaround
Establish a named escalation owner and escalation path to prevent multiple conflicting threads for single migration blockers
Include success metrics showing exception reduction, closure time, and policy drift visibility for board audit committee
Obtain a weekly dashboard showing exceptions opened, exceptions closed, sites migrated, and sites at risk
Obtain payment schedule in writing from procurement with finance approval before signature

business_drivers.statement: Reduce unmanaged access and cloud policy drift as business drivers for renewal, since every exception becomes a governance conversation
Board-level pressure to reduce highest-risk sites with informal access paths, not just count deployed sites
Board audit committee asked about unmanaged cloud access, requiring visible policy drift findings and remediation status
Regional operational friction around legacy sites with tight maintenance windows that cannot support standard migration timelines

objections.statement: Procurement challenged the uplift and requires better explanation of what changed
Legal asked for narrower liability wording to align with privacy team approval
Legal requested clarification on data retention language
Technical concern that older sites may require temporary bypasses that conflict with security goal
If dashboards are late, buyer may hold back signature until final week

competitor_mentions.statement: Competitor mentioned as cheaper but less integrated

commitments.statement: Northstar will confirm the first-wave sites and name regional approvers

Include policy reference line and attach approved data retention policy excerpt

conflicts.claim_a: In the March planning session, pilot sites should move first, with older appliances handled via a separate legacy-site plan to avoid making every exception look normal
conflicts.claim_b: As of May 2, Pavel Stone now wants the two legacy-appliance sites migrated before the pilot sites, reversing the pilot-first sequencing agreed in March
conflicts.assessment: Both claims cannot hold; Pavel Stone cannot have both endorsed the pilot-first approach in March and reversed it to legacy-first in May without an intervening decision. The evidence does not clarify whether Marco Devlin agrees with the reversal.
